newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - April 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Actress Pai Ping-ping urges police to quickly nab killer, or killers, of her daughter Pai Hsiao-yen.
U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright urges Taiwan and China to resume dialogues.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - Gangster organisation is behind killing of Pai Hsiao-yen.
Parliament lawmakers ask President Lee Teng-hui to apologise and Vice President Lien Chan to resign over murder of Pai Hsiao-yen.
LIBERTY TIMES - Police say up to nine gangsters may be involved in kidnapping and murder of Pai Hsiao-yen.
Vice President Lien Chan asks law authorities to set deadline for capture of Pai Hsiao-yen's killers.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Bank and four other industries to be incorporated under Labour Law starting tomorrow.
U.S. chip giant Intel Corp may bring big orders to Taiwan chipmakers.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Lee Yuan-tseh, president of Academia Sinica, says Taiwan society is too corrupt.
Japanese computer makers praise quality of Taiwan-made semiconductor products.
